steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I'm back. I found some bread and clean water. Craig's been running about most of the night, he needs to fill up his stomach...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Er, what's wrong with everyone? What... happened?

steps.name: Grieving Man
steps.text: It's her! She's the one who tipped the Victorian Army off... She killed Saoirse!

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: What... What are you talking about?!?!

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Saoirse... What happened to Saoirse?!

steps.name: Grieving Man
steps.text: You're asking? She's dead! You black-hearted Victorian soldier! You got close to her just so you could pluck intel from her own mouth, didn't you?

steps.name: Grieving Man
steps.text: And now she's been executed—are you happy?!

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I never even thought...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: How could this...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I'm sorry... I'm sorry... Saoirse...

steps.name: Grieving Man
steps.text: Save your tears! You've no right to be sad for her! And you've no right... to be standing here!

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I was sincere with her, always...

steps.name: Grieving Man
steps.text: Sincere? A Victorian soldier, telling us Tarans sincerity?

steps.name: Grieving Man
steps.text: What a joke for the ages!

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Aren't we all... countrymen?

steps.name: Grieving Man
steps.text: Countrymen? What do you know of our country?

steps.name: Grieving Man
steps.text: Have you eaten the grains we eat, spoken the language we speak, felt the pain we feel?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: But I've always wanted to help you...

steps.name: Grieving Man
steps.text: Don't come any closer! Put down your flag! You're not calling for backup on us!

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I don't want to... I wasn't...

steps.name: Grieving Man
steps.text: Get out of our land! Never again will the home of the Tarans need Victoria's ensign!

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: You want... me gone?

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: We've got no choice.

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: You saw how... I never even did any wrong, and yet... none of you would just let me go...

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: I think... Ronan was right, we have a chance now. If we can just win, then nobody will ever come hassling me or Craig again... *sob*...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Craig... do you...?

steps.name: Craig
steps.text: We don't need you!

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: A... stone?

a.text: 'Have you seen the looks in their eyes before?'
'In their eyes, no matter how you behave...'

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: So it was... me who never figured it out.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I should go.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: The troops are retreating in defeat. Over half the blocks in this city will very soon fall into the spectre force's hands.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: How'd they break so quick?! I was thinkin', even if their organization and trainin' was rock-bottom level, at least they could hold out until tomorrow mornin'.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: You noticed how that squad from the barracks behaved just now, didn't you?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I saw it. We were holdin' the stadium together, but then once the enemy came, they all ran for the rear in a flash. Would've been useless no matter how we held out.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: They seem to have completely lost their will to fight.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: That might be it. After all, it was a situation just now. The enemy shows up, the residents in refuge all cheer for 'em and open the gates in. Any soldier'd be a little deflated watchin' a scene like that.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: But Colonel Hamilton doesn't seem in any way like the kind who gives up this easily. He especially values County Hillock.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: The barracks might be at a disadvantage right now, but they didn't seem to be in any chaos at all when they retreated. They still had firm organization.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I can only believe that this present state still falls into the Colonel's plans. He has some other intent in this war situation.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Closest forces are County Kevin's barracks. If we sent out the signal for help, they could get here by evenin' soonest.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: ...Assuming they receive the signal in the first place.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Worried about problems with the comms system?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: It's our third day since coming here, and we still haven't received any news from Londinium. County Hillock is like a lone island at this moment.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: No problem, just a few grenades and a wee squad of mixed forces. I'll sort it out. This street's still safe for the time bein'.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Bagpipe... remember in training when you just joined us, I gave you two hours of weighted handstand push-ups as a punishment.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Course I'd never forget, Leader. Wasn't much of a bad punishment as far as I'm concerned, but for a while, I really thought you didn't like me too much.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I never told you why.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Actually, it was because you told me as you were reporting in, you'd stuffed mince pudding and blankets in your marching bag.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Eh? That's a hometown treat. It's good, honest.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: You said much the same at the time.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: On the day of the solo cross-country test, you were already starving when you came back, and you obviously kept food in your bag, but you still wouldn't eat it.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Couldn't really bear to... I was goin' to have it as a reward for myself, once the trainin' was over. Scoff it down at the happiest moment.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I once maintained that a person too attached to her home, unable to surmount the past, could not become a good officer.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: So, though your grades at Royal Guard were exceptional, and Instructor Slim spared no effort in recommending you to me, I still had doubts as to your potential.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: So that's what it was! But you've been awful nice to me since.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: You proved yourself.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I gradually came to understand. It's only because you have an indestructible attachment in you, that you could become who you are today, a most excellent Victorian soldier, someone to surpass me.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Bagpipe, what I say next, you need to listen well—

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: We have to give up on this block. I'm about to take Cello's group to a comms base in the northeast corner. We're hoping it hasn't been occupied by the spectre force yet.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: And you, go immediately to the contact station, find a Messenger, and ensure you find them a way out of the city too.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: If there's already no way left, then make one.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Bagpipe, I order you. Shy at no cost. You have to relay out what's happened in County Hillock.

steps.name: Busy Youth
steps.text: Dammit. The others are all with The Leader doing more meaningful things, and I get the rotten luck of sweeping up here...

steps.name: Busy Youth
steps.text: Funny now that I think about it. There's fighting going on all over. Why would The Leader insist I sweep clean around the statue?

steps.name: Busy Youth
steps.text: Huh? Who is it... What are you grabbing at me for?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Is this where... Saoirse died?

steps.name: Busy Youth
steps.text: Saoirse? You mean the traitor The Leader executed? Yeah, it was all her fault. She's dead, and you want me here bloody sweeping up these ashes...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: You mean, what you're sweeping is...

steps.name: Busy Youth
steps.text: Rubbish, nothing more.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: She... She was a good girl. To her family, to her friends... she was so warm. She gave... everything for this city.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Why? What... did she even do wrong? She teared up just reading romance novels—she'd never have it in her to harm anyone...

steps.name: Busy Youth
steps.text: Wh... What in the world's wrong with you?

steps.name: Busy Youth
steps.text: Do you sympathize with this traitor? Just who are you?!

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: She's not called 'traitor.' Her name is Saoirse.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: She shouldn't be lying here so alone. I'm taking her back home.

steps.name: Busy Youth
steps.text: You've got a screw loose. I'm leaving.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: What's happening over there?

steps.name: Busy Youth
steps.text: Sir! There's someone strange, crouching there, going on and on about taking the traitor home! I think she might be an enemy as well, and a traitor too!!

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: Alright, good on you for reporting.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: Hey, who are you?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: (...Saoirse, maybe you were wrong, and so was I.)

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: (You used your life to protect these people, and they didn't even care that you did. And they welcomed the rioters, too. The way this city's turned out now, they're not that innocent at all.)

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: Are you from the other side?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: The other side? I don't know anymore—which side I'm even stood on.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: Don't move! Any more, and your skull is—

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Dealt with yet another few.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Rabblesome dregs... hah, I'll take however many I can do in on the retreat.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Hey, Vouivre over there, have you seen more of them about?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: (...Dregs.)

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: (Calling Saoirse rubbish. Of course they're dregs.)

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: They just went running that way.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: We'll head right over—
It seemed as if I heard the residents' shrieks, and seemed too as if I'd heard nothing at all.
I only thought of bringing Saoirse away, but no matter how I tried to put the strength in my fingers, the ash would still slip and fall through the cracks.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Saoirse...
A hand reached out to me.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Time to get clear out, Jane.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Here, lemon tea. Warm up.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: If you want to cry, just let it out.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: ...I can't get the tears out.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: I can feel your anger. Do you hate them?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Perhaps...

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: You got those soldiers to grab a Taran who supports the riots. That make you feel any better?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Maybe, I hate myself even more.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: If... I didn't hand that slip over, Saoirse wouldn't have died, would she?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: But all I wanted was to stop a bigger conflict... I thought, so long as I stood up, I could change...

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: We wouldn't call it fate if it always went how we wanted.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Jane, can I tell you a story?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Go on. I'll try to listen.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: I'll keep it short.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Decades ago, when I was about your age... No, maybe a bit older, back when I worked for the Church—

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: You don't seem a thing like those Laterano clerics.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Years and experience are pretty good at changing a person.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: They had me arbitrating a war. Who the sides were, or why they were fighting, that's not important anymore. The parties responsible for getting the ball rolling are probably all dust anyway.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: I just remember, there was a city asking for my help. I told them to lay their weapons down, I was ready to be their go-between, and off I went for peace talks with a general from the side sieging the place.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: The people in the city really weren't up for it, with the whole 'surrendering to tyranny' thing, so I took some drastic measures to get them talking, but we still never came to an agreement, in the end.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: I gave up hope and left, bringing with me just a few who were willing to quit fighting, but the second day after I left, the city was breached.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Pretty much everyone who stayed ended up dead.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: I believe... a good chunk of them all thought, nearing death's door, I'd still come and protect them in the end. But I didn't.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Looking back, I guess I was on the other side. I was the sinister pretender who'd given them hope, gotten them massacred.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: But you're not!

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: You sure? Who can say?

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: After that, I renounced my appointment as a cardinal, and left Laterano.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: It sounds like you tried your best...

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Really? What if I kept at it, tried harder to stop the massacre that was coming?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Then you probably couldn't save a single one.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Or maybe I shouldn't have gone there with unrealistic hopes in the first place. Maybe I should've walked up and put a bullet in the head of the brute about to butcher an entire city.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Wouldn't that... have other consequences?

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: No one can tell you the consequences of opening fire before you do it.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: But still, are you telling me you'd stand by and watch—just let evil happen over and over, and over again?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: ...I wouldn't.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: You're right. No matter how I keep questioning myself... I don't regret it at all.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Bagpipe... I hope you can still make it.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Triangle?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: You came in at the right time. I'm about to dash for a communications center, position not far from here. You don't have to enter the city, we'll rendezvous directly at the outskirts—

steps.name: Triangle
steps.text: ...Leader.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: What happened to you?! You sound in awful shape! Were you wounded?

steps.name: Triangle
steps.text: Hah... not a... big issue... ahah... forget it, it's a little big. But no need... to fuss about me.

steps.name: Triangle
steps.text: Leader, I don't have much time. We've definitely found what we were looking for.

steps.name: Triangle
steps.text: These Originium products were sent to the artillery battalion.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Artillery battalion?! The barracks' one?

steps.name: Triangle
steps.text: Yes, absolutely. We're in here right now.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: The barracks have already been breached by the spectre force?!

steps.name: Triangle
steps.text: To be honest, I don't know.

steps.name: Triangle
steps.text: Another thing you need to know. The Originium products we found had all gone through modification.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: What kind of modification?

steps.name: Triangle
steps.text: I only came by a part of it. Their structures aren't whole, someone's taken out the parts with active Originium... Do you still remember the serial bombing case at Stockton?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: The offending group created a huge amount of incompletely combusting bombs, and caused grave Originium dust pollution in the core district, in retaliation against the government.

steps.name: Triangle
steps.text: Right... hah... you get what I mean.

steps.name: Triangle
steps.text: They have us surrounded... we're out of luck hiding...

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: And Snare? The others?!

steps.name: Triangle
steps.text: Snare's... next to me. There's a bolt clean through her heart... she went without too much pain, fortunately. Bass and Mandolin are still in the warehouse. Sorry. I couldn't bring them...

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: You did all you could. You're a fine leader.

steps.name: Triangle
steps.text: Am I, then...? Surely not as good as you, Leader.

steps.name: Triangle
steps.text: These hostiles... they're bizarre. They use weapons just like ours. And on top of that, I can hear... familiar call-outs...

steps.name: Triangle
steps.text: Just who... is our enemy?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: That's not important, Triangle. You all come back alive for me, you hear that? This is an order!

steps.name: Triangle
steps.text: Hah... got it, Leader. I'll keep it in mind.
